statement: Let $A\to P$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in P$ be a *Koszul-regular sequence* (its Koszul complex is exact in positive degrees). Assume $B=P/(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ is flat over $A$. Suppose $g_1,\ldots,g_n\in P\otimes_AB$ form a Koszul-regular sequence and generate the kernel of the natural multiplication map $P\otimes_AB\to B$. Choose elements $g_{ij}\in P\otimes_AB$ such that $f_i\otimes1=\sum_{j=1}^n g_{ij}g_j$. Let $\bar\delta\in B\otimes_AB$ be the image of $\det(g_{ij})$ under the map $P\otimes_AB\to B\otimes_AB$. Then the annihilator ideal $J=\operatorname{Ann}_{B\otimes_AB}(\ker(B\otimes_AB\xrightarrow\mu B))$ is the principal ideal $(\bar\delta)$ of $B\otimes_AB$.
hypotheses: Two Koszul-regular sequences f_i in P and g_j in P⊗_A B; B=P/(f) is A-flat; g generate the kernel of P⊗_A B→B; matrix gij expresses f⊗1.
conclusions: The diagonal multiplication-kernel annihilator is generated by the image of det(gij).
semantic_review_note: For A→P, a Koszul-regular sequence f_i cutting out B flat over A, and a second Koszul-regular sequence g_j generating the multiplication kernel in P⊗_A B with f_i⊗1=Σ g_{ij}g_j, the annihilator of the diagonal ideal in B⊗_A B is generated by det(g_{ij}). Both regularity hypotheses and the exact ring containing the annihilator remain.

\label{lemma-quasi-finite-complete-intersection}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $n \geq 1$ and
$h, f_1, \ldots, f_n \in A[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$.
Set $B = A[x_1, \ldots, x_n, 1/h]/(f_1, \ldots, f_n)$.
Assume that $B$ is quasi-finite over $A$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $B$ is flat over $A$ and $A \to B$ is a relative local complete
intersection,
\item the annihilator $J$ of $I = \Ker(B \otimes_A B \to B)$
is free of rank $1$ over $B$,
\item the Noether different of $B$ over $A$ is generated
by $\det(\partial f_i/\partial x_j)$ in $B$.
\end{enumerate}
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\geq1$, and $h,f_1,\ldots,f_n\in A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. Put $B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n,1/h]/(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ and suppose $A\to B$ is quasi-finite. Let $\mu:B\otimes_AB\to B$ denote multiplication and $I=\ker\mu$, $J=\operatorname{Ann}_{B\otimes_AB}(I)$ (viewed as a $B$-module via $\mu$). The *Noether different* is $\mathfrak D^{\mathrm N}_{B/A}=\mu(J)\subseteq B$. Then (1) $B$ is flat over $A$ and $A\to B$ is a relative local complete intersection; (2) $J$ is a free $B$-module of rank one; and (3) $\mathfrak D^{\mathrm N}_{B/A}$ is generated by the image in $B$ of the Jacobian determinant $\det(\partial f_i/\partial x_j)$.
hypotheses: A ring, n equations in n variables localized at h, and resulting B quasi-finite over A.
conclusions: B is flat and lci; the Noether J module is rank-one free; Noether different is Jacobian determinant ideal.
semantic_review_note: For B=A[x_1,...,x_n,1/h]/(f_1,...,f_n) quasi-finite over A, the source asserts all three: A→B flat and relative lci; diagonal annihilator J free rank one over B; and its Noether different generated by the Jacobian determinant. All three and the special presentation are retained.
